h1: SEO Agency in New York: win Astoria before you try Manhattan
metaTitle: SEO Agency in New York: Borough-Level, Not Citywide
metaDescription: New York intent is neighbourhood-level. Winning Astoria beats losing Manhattan. We name the categories we decline first, then scope the rest honestly.
answer: New York search happens at neighbourhood level. People search "dentist astoria" and "movers park slope", not "dentist new york". Winning one neighbourhood is achievable on a mid-size retainer. Winning a citywide head term in personal injury or insurance is not, at almost any budget we could honestly quote you.
takeaways: There are categories in New York we turn down. They're listed below, before anything else on this page, because the alternative is taking your money for a fight we'd lose.
Neighbourhood beats borough beats city. Astoria, Park Slope, Bushwick, Flushing and Riverdale are the units of demand — not "NYC".
Your competition on informational queries isn't other agencies. It's Eater, Time Out, The Infatuation and The Strategist, and you don't out-publish them. You get cited by them.
A ₹75,000 retainer converts to roughly US$850. That buys real work in India and would not staff a US team for a week. Both facts are true at once.

sections.h2: The New York categories we turn down
body: Most agency pages open with what they can do. This one opens with what we can't, because in New York the gap between those two lists is wider than anywhere else we work, and every month somebody enquires from one of these categories.
If your business is in one of the following, a mid-size retainer is not a serious answer and we will say so on the first call:
numbered: **Personal injury and mass tort.** The incumbents have fifteen-plus years of domain history, thousands of pages, in-house SEO teams and litigation budgets behind them. This is the most expensive keyword category in the world and the reason is that a single case pays for the year.
**Insurance.** Same shape. National carriers and comparison sites hold every commercial query, and they buy the paid results underneath as well.

**Addiction treatment and behavioural health.** Beyond the competition, this is a YMYL category where Google's quality expectations are strict and the referral market has a genuine history of bad actors. It needs a specialist who knows the compliance ground.
**Consumer lending, credit repair and payday.** Regulated, heavily spammed, and the winners are publishers with review-site economics rather than lenders.

**Locksmiths, emergency dispatch and similar 24-hour trades.** The map pack in these categories has a long-documented fake-listing problem in New York. Competing honestly against dishonest listings is a game of endurance, not of SEO skill.
**Interstate moving companies.** Lead-broker economics, aggressive directories, and a market where your organic ranking competes with someone paying more for the same click.

callout.title: What to do instead if you're in one of these
callout.body: Hire a US specialist who lives inside the category, or run paid with a tight geographic radius and accept the cost per lead. What you should not do is take a cheaper offshore retainer, including ours, and expect it to compete. Anyone who tells you otherwise is selling you eighteen months of invoices.

body: New York is five boroughs and several hundred named neighbourhoods, and New Yorkers navigate by the neighbourhood. Someone in Astoria does not consider a dentist in Bay Ridge to be in the same city, functionally, even though both are in the same city, literally. That's a forty-minute subway ride with a transfer.

So the query is "dentist astoria", "physical therapy park slope", "tax accountant flushing". These terms have modest volume individually and enormous volume collectively, and almost nobody builds for them properly because building for them means writing dozens of pages that are genuinely different from each other rather than one page with the name swapped.
Here's what each query shape actually returns, and what you can realistically do about it.

sections.h2: How many Google profiles a multi-site New York business should have
body: The rule is one profile per staffed location, and New York generates more edge cases against that rule than any city we work in.
A restaurant group with three rooms in three neighbourhoods gets three profiles, three landing pages, three phone numbers, three review streams. Straightforward. It gets harder from there.
bullets: **Suite numbers in a shared building.** Legitimate if you're genuinely there during your stated hours. A midtown building with two hundred businesses is fine; a mailbox service inside it is not.
**Co-working memberships.** Not a location, however much the membership costs. If the desk isn't yours and isn't staffed by you, run as a service-area business instead.

**Practitioners.** Doctors, dentists, lawyers and therapists can hold an individual profile alongside the practice's profile — public-facing professionals are treated differently from staff. Used properly this is one of the few legitimate ways to hold more than one listing at one address.

**Departments.** A hospital's emergency department and its cardiology clinic can be listed separately where they're genuinely distinct and separately reachable. Most businesses invent departments to game this. Google notices.

callout.title: The number that actually matters
callout.body: Not how many profiles you hold — how many of them have more than twenty genuine reviews from the last twelve months. In New York's local pack, review recency and volume do more work than almost anything you can do on the page. If you can only fix one thing this quarter, fix the review flow.

sections.h2: You're not competing with agencies, you're competing with publishers
body: This is the part that surprises founders. For any informational or "best of" query in New York, the ranking pages belong to Eater NY, Time Out New York, The Infatuation, New York Magazine's The Strategist and a long tail of well-staffed local publishers. They have editorial teams, decades of domain history and links from everywhere.

You will not out-publish them, and the strategy of trying — grinding out sixty blog posts a year to compete on "best brunch in the west village" — is how most New York content budgets die. The volume of content required to compete head-on with a US publisher is a newsroom, not a retainer.

The work that does pay is narrower and duller. Pages only you can write: your pricing, your process, your service area, your comparison against the alternative, your answers to the six questions every customer asks before booking. Those rank because nobody else can write them, and they convert because they're what the buyer wanted. Then digital PR to earn a mention in the publishers' lists rather than fighting them for the slot — the mechanics of that are in [digital PR services](/services/digital-pr-services).

callout.title: Read this before you get excited about the number
callout.body: US agencies price off US salaries, so a full-team New York retainer generally starts in the low thousands of dollars a month. Ours doesn't, and that is a cost-of-living difference, not a magic one. What it buys you is a competent team on a neighbourhood-level build. What it does not buy you is a fight in the categories at the top of this page, and it does not buy you someone who can walk into a meeting in Flatiron. New York is nine and a half hours behind India in summer — our 6:30pm is your 9am, and that's the overlap you get.

sections.h2: What the ninety days actually measure
body: The first fortnight is a technical crawl, a Search Console and analytics review, a neighbourhood-level keyword build, and a written baseline: your trailing-90-day count of qualified leads from organic search, frozen on day one.

Then that number is the contract. Beat it in ninety days or we keep working free until we do. We never promise a ranking position for a keyword — nobody controls Google's index, Google's own guidance warns against exactly that promise, and in a city where the map pack changes between Astoria and Long Island City a "position" isn't even a single number.

Two definitions we settle in writing before day one, because New York breaks both of them. First, what counts as qualified — form fills from bots and from lead-resellers are a real volume problem on US sites, and a baseline that counts them is a baseline you can beat dishonestly. Second, what counts as organic — if a meaningful share of your traffic arrives via a marketplace, a booking platform or an aggregator, we agree upfront how that's attributed. If we can't agree a clean number, we say so and don't take the work. We take three clients a month, which is the only reason a guarantee like this survives contact with reality. The argument for and against hiring offshore at all is laid out in [Indian agency versus international agency](/compare/indian-seo-agency-vs-international-agency).

faqs.q: Why won't you take personal injury or insurance clients in New York?
faqs.a: Because we'd lose. Those categories have incumbents with fifteen years of domain history, thousands of pages and in-house teams, funded by case values that justify it. No retainer we could honestly quote competes there. If you're in one of those categories, hire a US specialist in the vertical or run tightly targeted paid.

faqs.q: Should I target Manhattan or my own neighbourhood?
faqs.a: Your neighbourhood, then the ones next to it. New Yorkers search by neighbourhood — Astoria, Park Slope, Flushing, Bushwick — and those terms are winnable with one genuinely specific page each. Citywide head terms are held by aggregators and national groups, and you'll rank for them as a side effect of winning twenty neighbourhoods.

faqs.q: How many Google Business Profiles should a multi-location NYC business have?
faqs.a: One per genuinely staffed location, each with its own landing page, phone number and reviews. Co-working desks and mailbox addresses don't qualify and get suspended. Individual doctors, dentists and lawyers can hold practitioner profiles alongside the practice listing — that's the main legitimate exception.

faqs.q: How much does an SEO agency in New York cost?
faqs.a: US agencies price off US salaries, so a full-team retainer generally starts in the low thousands of dollars a month. Ours is ₹75,000/mo, roughly US$850 at a rupee–dollar rate near ₹88, with smaller sites from ₹40,000. Ex-GST, ad spend billed separately with zero media markup.

faqs.q: Can I outrank Eater or Time Out for New York queries?
faqs.a: Realistically, no — they have editorial teams, decades of domain history and links from everywhere. The productive move is to get cited in their lists rather than compete for the slot, and to build the pages only you can write: pricing, process, service area, and the questions every customer asks before booking.

faqs.q: Does the time difference make an Indian agency unworkable for New York?
faqs.a: It makes it slower, not unworkable. New York runs nine and a half to ten and a half hours behind India, so the overlap is the start of your day and the end of ours. It works with a fixed weekly call in that window and written decisions. If you need same-hour responsiveness or in-person meetings, hire locally.
